 What Aftermath Should Write About GTA VI, According To My Email
 So many press releases
 By 
 Riley MacLeod

 Ahead of GTA VI ’s New Zealand launch, Aftermath contributor Jackson Ryan warned that we’re about to see the “stupidest week in history.” As the game slowly becomes available across the world, media outlets flail to find any and all ways to turn that hype into traffic and thereby money, and any individual or company who can find the slightest connection to GTA VI tries to leverage the game to get some attention.
 Ever since the game’s reveal, Aftermath’s inboxes have been full of pitches about it. These aren’t from writers with something to say about the game (though there’s plenty of those too), but from companies, research firms, and self-styled experts in a variety of fields who want us to say something about them on our site. This isn’t a practice unique to GTA VI –our inboxes are regularly crammed with this stuff–but the hype around the game has led to a particular kind of desperate brainrot.
 Here’s some of the stories these folks have thought should appear on our website:
 A list of the world’s most “GTA-obsessed” countries
 The countries “waiting for” the game the most
 A report claiming that GTA VI is the most anticipated launch among female gamers
 Data claiming that the game isn’t in fact the most anticipated
 The states where you’d need the most and least work hours to afford a copy of GTA VI 
 Data on the service industries most affected by people allegedly calling out to play
 A “men’s health expert” on how men can stay healthy during the game’s launch week
 How playing the game could affect men’s testosterone levels
 How playing the game could affect couples’ health, which is basically the same pitch as the testosterone one
 Why video games like GTA are actually good for your health
 What GTA characters would look like if they came from each US state, as conceived of by AI
 An AI company on why players will actually still play other games
 Which real world cities players think GTA VII should take place in
 Some of these pitches have actually been picked up by gaming sites, which is a real self-own by traffic-obsessed leadership. Other sites have spun up similar ideas seemingly all on their own, particularly, as Jackson wrote, stories about alleged sick days and other hypothetical economic impacts of a lot of people playing a game. And there’s also the usual embarrassment of non-gaming outlets parading their shock that video games both exist and are popular. 
 I can’t totally fault these various experts and companies for firing their ideas our way; like I said, it’s a long-standing practice, and clearly it must work enough times for them to see some benefit in continuing to do it. (Pornhub has been doing it for ages.) The fact that some of these stories have actually made it to the page are, if anything, a symptom of what happens when gaming outlets close or lose experienced writers, or mainstream outlets don’t take games seriously until they have to. Hopefully now that the game is starting to make its way to people, there’ll be more actual stories, or we’ll at least find out if anyone really called in sick and toppled the global economy.
